description: Get a USGS site's current reading ranked against its full period-of-record daily-mean percentiles for the same calendar day — a "how unusual is this" percentileClass (record-high to record-low), not a flood-stage or drought determination (this tool fetches no authoritative thresholds). Rankings follow the water level: for a depth-to-water code (72019) a shallower depth ranks higher. The reading is instantaneous but the percentiles are daily-mean, so the ranking is approximate (see historicalContext.comparisonBasis). When the record is too short to rank, returns the reading with historicalContext=null instead of an error. A reading USGS reports as no data (a seasonal, discontinued, dry, or malfunctioning gage) returns an empty currentValue with the qualifiers naming why, and is not ranked. When the site measures the parameter with several sensors (methods), one reading is used and named by methodId/methodDescription — from a sensor the statistics hold a daily-mean series for when one is, otherwise the most recent across them; water_get_readings lists every method. Use water_find_sites and water_list_parameters to resolve inputs.

parameterCd.description: 5-digit USGS parameter code (e.g. "00060" for discharge, "00065" for gage height). Use water_list_parameters to discover codes.

site.description: USGS site number (8–15 digits, e.g. "01646500" for Potomac River at Little Falls). Use water_find_sites to discover valid site numbers.

name: water_get_conditions

currentDateTime.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the most recent observation.

currentValue.description: Most recent observed value as a string — for a depth-to-water code, the depth as measured. Empty string when USGS reported no value for the reading — qualifiers then give the reason, and historicalContext does not rank it. A method with a measured latest reading is preferred over one whose latest reading has no value.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `no_data_for_parameter`: No reading came back for the site and parameter in the last two hours: the site does not exist, never measured the parameter, or reported nothing in that window. `invalid_request`: The USGS Water Data API rejected the reading request. Inputs are validated before the call, so this surfaces a value that is well-formed but unacceptable upstream. `upstream_error`: The USGS Water Data API answered the reading request with a 5xx error or a response it could not read, and retrying did not clear it. A statistics failure does not raise this — it is reported as historicalContextStatus "unavailable". `upstream_timeout`: The reading did not arrive within the budget this call shares across its requests. A statistics timeout is reported as historicalContextStatus "unavailable". Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

comparisonBasis.description: Fixed disclosure that percentileClass ranks an instantaneous reading against approved daily-mean percentiles — a cross-granularity approximation, not a flood-stage or drought determination. For a depth-below-surface code it also says the depth is ranked as a water level. Present whenever historicalContext is non-null.

methodMatched.description: True when the percentiles come from the daily-mean series computed from the reported sensor's own series (methodId), linked by time-series ID. False when that sensor has no daily-mean series in the statistics and the site's only series with percentiles for the day was used instead (note says so) — the percentiles may then come from a different sensor or location than the reading.

p05.description: 5th percentile of water level in unitCode for this calendar month+day, based on the period of record — for a depth-below-surface code, the deepest of these depths. Null if that threshold is unpublished.

p10.description: 10th percentile value in unitCode for this calendar month+day. Null if unavailable.

p25.description: 25th percentile (lower quartile) in unitCode. Null if unavailable.

p50.description: Median (50th percentile) in unitCode for this calendar month+day. Null if unavailable.

p75.description: 75th percentile (upper quartile) in unitCode. Null if unavailable.

p95.description: 95th percentile of water level in unitCode for this calendar month+day — for a depth-below-surface code, the shallowest of these depths. Null if unpublished.

percentileClass.description: Classification of the water level relative to the full period-of-record: record-high (≥ p95), above-normal (p75–p95), normal (p25–p75), below-normal (p10–p25), low (p05–p10), record-low (< p05). For a depth-below-surface code (72019, 30210, 99019, 72276) a shallower depth is a higher water level, so a depth at or shallower than p95 is record-high and one deeper than p05 is record-low. Decided by the thresholds published: with p95 blank a reading at or past p75 is above-normal, and with p10 or p05 blank a reading short of p25 or p10 is below-normal or low. normal requires both p25 and p75; a value the published thresholds cannot place is unknown, as is a reading USGS reported as no data (currentValue empty). See percentileLabel for the threshold in plain language.

percentileLabel.description: Plain-language threshold for percentileClass (e.g. "25th–75th percentile"). When the class was decided without an unpublished threshold, the label names it (e.g. "≥ 75th percentile; 95th not published") — the value may lie past it. An unknown class names the published thresholds either side and the blank ones between (e.g. "25th–95th percentile; 75th not published"), or, for a reading with no value, says so and names its qualifiers. The record-high and record-low classes mark percentile-of-record extremes (≥ p95 / < p05), not verified all-time records — this field says so where the class name does not. For a depth-below-surface code the label also says the depth is ranked as a water level.

periodOfRecord.description: First and last water year of approved daily means for this calendar day, the years the percentiles are computed from (e.g. "1931–2026").

statSeriesDescription.description: Description of that daily-mean series, composed as methodDescription is (e.g. "From multiparameter sonde", "[BASE GAGE]"). Null when blank.

statSeriesId.description: Time-series ID of the daily-mean series the percentiles were computed from. When methodMatched is true, that series is computed from the instantaneous series named by methodId.

historicalContext.description: Historical percentile context for the observation's calendar day. Non-null only when historicalContextStatus is "available"; see that field for why it is otherwise absent.

historicalContextStatus.description: Why historicalContext is or is not populated. 'available': percentiles for the observation's calendar day are present. 'no_matching_day': the reported sensor's daily-mean series has an approved record but no percentiles for that calendar day. 'no_matching_method': several daily-mean series have percentiles for the day and none is computed from the reported sensor's series, so no series is picked to rank against (note lists them). 'no_record': no daily-mean percentiles exist for this site, parameter, and calendar day — a new site, a record too short, or a series with only daily maximum or minimum statistics. 'unavailable': a statistics or series-metadata request failed (note says why) — an upstream failure, not a statement about the site's record; call again later.

methodDescription.description: Description of that sensor series: its sublocation, with its web description in brackets (e.g. "From multiparameter sonde", "AUXILIARY GAGE"). Null when both are blank, as for the default series at most single-sensor sites.

methodId.description: Time-series ID of the instantaneous sensor series the current reading comes from, as water_get_readings returns it. When the site reports the parameter from several, a series with a measured latest reading is preferred, then one the statistics hold a daily-mean series for (so reading and percentiles come from one sensor), then the most recent, then the site's default sensor (methodDescription null) over a labeled one such as an auxiliary gage. Null only when the series carries no ID.

note.description: Informational note explaining why historicalContext is null or incomplete, that USGS reported no value for the current reading, or which daily-mean series the percentiles came from when methodMatched is false. Absent when the reading is measured and ranked against its own sensor's daily-mean series.

parameterCd.description: 5-digit USGS parameter code that was queried (e.g. "00060").

parameterName.description: Parameter description from the USGS parameter-code catalog, with units (e.g. "Discharge, cubic feet per second").

qualifiers.description: Data qualifiers for the current reading. When currentValue is empty they name why USGS has no value (e.g. seasonal, discontinued, dry, equipment malfunction).

items.description: A USGS data qualifier for the reading (e.g. "P" = provisional).

unitCode.description: Unit of measure for currentValue and the historical percentiles (e.g. "ft3/s", "ft").

title: Water Get Conditions
